parts:
Dear everyone?

messages.author: bfa43814f6ba1969
messages.subject: Re: PLS-Program?
parts:
Hi

R packages for PLS include matrixpls, plspm, and semPLS. matrixpls understands lavaan model syntax whereas the others have their own model specification format.

But if you want a useful method, I do not think that PLS is a good choice at all. For starters, check out your recent paper and the references therein:

Rönkkö, M., McIntosh, C. N., & Antonakis, J. (2015). On the Adoption of Partial Least Squares in Psychological Research: Caveat Emptor. Personality and Individual Differences, forthcoming. Retrieved from https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280083330_On_the_Adoption_of_Partial_Least_Squares_in_Psychological_Research_Caveat_Emptor

or this editorial (it should be out soon):

Ketokivi, M., & Guide, D. (2015). Notes from the editors: Redefining some methodological criteria for the journal. Journal of Operations Management, forthcoming.


Mikko

messages.author: bfa43814f6ba1969
messages.subject: Re: PLS-Program?
parts:
Hi,

This goes a bit off topic from the list, but Geoff raises a good question. It is clear that PLS use is increasing because it is being actively promoted, not because the method has any merits. Here is our recent take on the issue:

Rönkkö, M., McIntosh, C. N., & Antonakis, J. (2015). On the adoption of partial least squares in psychological research: Caveat emptor. Personality and Individual Differences, (87), 76–84. http://doi.org/10.1016/j.paid.2015.07.019

(We have another similar paper coming out later this year. I will post it on my research gate profile once the paper is out.)

One might also ask why PLS is virtually absent from the mainstream social sciences research methods literature. 

Mikko

messages.author: 601aa4bb4d2fbfcf
messages.subject: Re: PLS-Program?
parts:
Yes, PLS path modeling is hugely popular, if the rate of acceleration in use over the past 15 years is any indication.

And the proactive promotion of PLS path modeling as a useful and valid quantitative analysis technique by top scholars, editors-in-chief and senior editors of top research journals in multiple fields over the past decade certainly has not impeded that prolific uptake.

To facilitate and accommodate this continued burgeoning demand in education and training on PLS path modeling for research data analysis purposes, we are establishing a platform of certified courses that teach the latest advancements in PLS path modeling as referenced in the top research journals over the past 5 years. This program will offer perpetual access and certificates of completion for each course.

They will be available by the time school begins again here in the United States, and in no cases will enrollment in any certified, multi-dozen session course cost more than $19 USD, and often less.

Best, Geoff Hubona
